{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Chris H. Greene''' is an American physicist and the [[Albert Overhauser]] Distinguished Professor of Physics and Astronomy at [[Purdue University]].<ref name=Purdue2019>{{cite press release |title=Purdue physics, astronomy professor elected to prestigious National Academy of Sciences |url=https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/releases/2019/Q2/purdue-physics,-astronomy-professor-elected-to-prestigious-national-academy-of-sciences.html |publisher=Purdue University |date=30 April 2019}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2019.<ref name=Purdue2019 />

== Early life and education ==
Greene was born in 1954 in [[Lincoln, Nebraska]].<ref name="AIP-PHN">{{cite web |title=Christopher Henry Greene |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11512011.html |work=Physics history Network |publisher=American Institute of Physics |accessdate=25 September 2019}}</ref> He earned a bachelor of science in physics from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] in 1976. He entered the graduate program at the [[University of Chicago]], earning a master's degree in 1977 and a doctorate in 1980.<ref name=Purdue2019 /> His thesis, under [[Ugo Fano]], was titled "Doubly-excited states of the alkaline earth atoms".<ref name="AIP-PHN" /><ref name="Greene1981">{{cite journal |last1=Greene |first1=Chris H. |title=Doubly excited states of the akaline-earth{{sic|hide=y}} atoms |journal=Physical Review A |volume=23 |issue=2 |year=1981 |pages=661–678 |issn=0556-2791 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.23.661|bibcode=1981PhRvA..23..661G }}</ref> He spent a postdoctoral year at [[Stanford University]] working with [[Richard Zare]].<ref name=APS2010>{{cite web |title=2010 Davisson-Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics Recipient |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Greene&first_nm=Chris&year=2010 |publisher=American Physical Society |accessdate=25 September 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1981, Greene was appointed assistant professor of physics at [[Louisiana State University]]. He was promoted to associate professor in 1984 and full professor in 1988. He accepted a position at the [[University of Colorado, Boulder]], in 1989 as professor of physics. Greene held various leadership positions during his tenure there including director of the Center for Theoretical Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics at JILA and the University of Colorado (1991–1999), JILA fellow (1989–2012), JILA chair (2005–2006), and Arts and Science Professor of Distinction (2011–2012). While at the University of Colorado, he was elected chair of the Division of Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics (DAMOP) of the American Physical Society in 2002-2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=Proceedings of the American Physical Society |url=https://www.aps.org/units/damop/history/index.cfm |website=APS Physics History}}</ref> In 2012, he was appointed distinguished professor of physics and astronomy at Purdue University, subsequently titled the [[Albert Overhauser]] Distinguished Professor of Physics and Astronomy.

== Awards and honors ==
* 1990 [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |website=APS Fellow Archive}}</ref>
* 1991 [[I. I. Rabi Award]] of the American Physical Society<ref>{{cite web |title=Rabi Prize in Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/rabi.cfm |website=APS Physics}}</ref>
* 2007 University of California at Berkeley, Visiting Miller Professorship<ref>{{cite web |title=In the News 2018-2019 |url=https://miller.berkeley.edu/news |website=Miller Institute Miller News}}</ref>
* 2007 Alexander von Humboldt Research Award for Senior U.S. Scientists
* 2010 [[Davisson–Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics]] of the American Physical Society<ref>{{cite web |title=2010 Davisson-Germer Prize |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Greene&first_nm=Chris&year=2010 |website=APS Physics}}</ref>
* 2013 [[Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging|Hamburg Prize for Theoretical Physics]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Giant Molecules Win Purdue Professor the Hamburg Prize |url=https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/releases/2013/Q3/giant-molecules-win-purdue-professor-the-hamburg-prize-for-theoretical-physics.html |website=Purdue University}}</ref>
* 2019 Elected member, National Academy of Sciences<ref name=Purdue2019 />
